subject.title: macOS: Gateway daemon PATH excludes user bin dirs (nix, bun, local, etc.)

question: Should macOS managed Gateway services continue to use only the canonical LaunchAgent PATH, or should OpenClaw add an explicit operator-controlled way to include user-bin directories for tools such as Nix and Bun?
rationale: Current tests and Gateway doctor docs encode a hardened macOS PATH policy, while the Nix docs and the report describe a supported macOS launchd Nix PATH expectation.

options.title: Keep Hardened Default, Add Explicit Opt-In
options.body: Preserve the current LaunchAgent default and add a documented, tested operator-controlled path for user-bin or extra service PATH directories.

options.title: Change macOS Default
options.body: Include user-bin directories by default on macOS, accepting the broader PATH-hijack surface for service child processes.

options.title: Documentation-Only Correction
options.body: Leave service PATH behavior unchanged and update the Nix docs to stop promising macOS launchd Nix discovery.

recommendation.title: Keep Hardened Default, Add Explicit Opt-In
recommendation.body: Preserve the current LaunchAgent default and add a documented, tested operator-controlled path for user-bin or extra service PATH directories.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical macOS service PATH policy commit makes steipete the clearest available routing candidate for this service PATH trust decision.
